summary: Frontend-only iteration for the wall-clock timer + Session Recap changes. Verified end-to-end in the web preview with mobile viewport (390x844) and the seeded ui-test-user token. (1) Timer screen loads clean, banner copy correctly reads '🔒 Focus Lock is on / The timer keeps running with your screen off — but opening another app kills your tree. Quick interruptions under a minute are forgiven.' matching the new screen-off-allowed rule. (2) Started a Custom 1-minute session — FocusLockOverlay opened immediately with locked-timer-display showing 00:59. Fired a visibilitychange→hidden for ~6s then →visible: focus-forgiven-banner appeared and the locked timer kept ticking (00:59 → 00:51 over ~8 real seconds), confirming the wall-clock endAtRef path with awaySec<=60 forgiveness works and the timer does NOT reset while backgrounded. (3) Let the session run to completion (~55s more). SessionRecap slid up automatically with all required testIDs populated — session-recap-screen, recap-xp='+2', recap-minutes='1', recap-streak='🔥 2', recap-today='2', recap-growth='Your tree is now at the sapling stage 🌿'. recap-close-button dismissed the modal cleanly (no black screen); the underlying timer-screen was fully interactive after close (preset-25 visible/clickable), focus-locked-screen was also gone, focus-history-card gained a new row, and focus-lock-streak incremented from 1 → 2 (persisted in Mongo user.focus_lock_streak). Zero JS console errors during the full flow. (4) Code inspection of the remaining paths: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/timer.tsx L127-163 correctly recomputes remaining from endAtRef on AppState 'active' and auto-completes when Date.now() >= endAt, so a >60s background where endAt already passed will call handleComplete(duration) rather than killTree — matches the review request. Web fallback for isScreenLocked (screenLock.ts L15-22) returns null on web ⇒ lockedAwayRef.current stays false ⇒ the >60s w/ Focus Lock on branch still calls killTree() as before (regression preserved). (5) sessionNotifications.ts unsupported() correctly no-ops on web and in Expo Go (Platform.OS==='web' || Constants.appOwnership==='expo'), scheduleNotificationAsync for ONGOING_ID uses trigger:null (sticky-ish 'ends at HH:MM' body) and completion uses DATE trigger at endAt; stopSessionNotifications dismisses ONGOING_ID and cancels all scheduled — called from clearTimer() so give-up, stop, and natural completion all clean up. No crashes seen when starting/stopping in the preview. (6) Regression: give-up path in FocusLockOverlay still exists (give-up-button → give-up-confirm-modal → give-up-confirm-button → killTree → focus-lock-death-modal) via code inspection; focus-history-card + focus-streak-card visibly updated after the run. Deprecated-package sweep clean (expo-notifications ~0.32.17, expo-screen-detector 0.1.1, expo-keep-awake ~15.0.8; no expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch). Cleanup verified in Mongo: plant_f950c13f4790 Oakley II still is_current+alive, ui-test-user focus_lock_enabled+notifications_enabled+strict_lock_enabled all true.
critical_code_review_comments: timer.tsx L126-163 — AppState listener correctly implements wall-clock timing: on 'active' it (a) auto-completes if endAtRef has passed, (b) resyncs remaining from endAt, (c) still applies the 60s grace / kill-tree logic gated by lockEnabledRef, and (d) forgives any absence when lockedAwayRef indicates the screen was off. Clean, single-source-of-truth via endAtRef.

timer.tsx L192-218 — beginSession sets endAtRef BEFORE starting the interval and BEFORE startSessionNotifications, so the ongoing notification and completion notification always use the same wall-clock end time as the AppState resync logic. Good.

timer.tsx L165-190 — handleComplete defers the recap by 550ms on iOS (120ms elsewhere) so the FocusLockOverlay Modal has time to dismiss before SessionRecap Modal mounts. This is the well-known iOS 'two Modals in a row = black screen' avoidance and it matches the iteration_14 give-up/death-modal fix.

sessionNotifications.ts L8 — unsupported() = Platform.OS==='web' || Constants.appOwnership==='expo' correctly no-ops in web preview AND Expo Go, so real notifications only fire in a native/dev build. Permission handling is graceful (silent return if denied). stopSessionNotifications also no-ops on unsupported and uses cancelAllScheduledNotificationsAsync which is a bit broad — if the app later schedules unrelated notifications (streak reminders, etc.) they'd also be cancelled at session end. Not a bug today, worth remembering.

screenLock.ts L15-22 — returns null on web / when the native module is unavailable, and the caller correctly treats only `=== true` as 'screen was off', so the web fallback preserves the pre-existing >60s-away-kills-tree behaviour. Solid.

SessionRecap.tsx — clean Modal, all six required testIDs (session-recap-screen, recap-xp, recap-minutes, recap-streak, recap-today, recap-growth conditional on stage, recap-close-button). Nothing to fix.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the flows executed (timer start, <60s bg forgiveness, natural completion + recap + dismiss + interactive timer + history/streak update)
